channel.title: # 🇱🇰 This Week in Sri Lanka
channel.description: Generated by gpt-5 from 316 English News Articles published between 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-02.

item.title: Parliament approved the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution by a two‑thirds majority.
item.description: The law raised the retirement ages of apex court judges by two years and capped the top judge’s tenure at six years. It also expanded the intermediate appellate bench by five seats, with the top court having held that the bill needed only a special majority and not a referendum. Backers said keeping senior benches intact a little longer would help clear backlogs, while critics warned about perceptions of judicial independence. Street demonstrations and courtroom challenges underscored the political stakes around tenure, appointments, and case flow.

item.title: The Monetary Policy Board kept the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR — the short‑term policy interest rate used to signal stance) at 8.75%.
item.description: The central bank projected headline inflation to stay in high single digits through the first quarter of 2027 before easing toward its 5% target, after prices held at 8.0% year‑on‑year in September for a second month. Output expanded 4.7% in the first half, while gross official reserves stood at $6.9 billion at end‑August after net foreign‑exchange purchases. Officials cited earlier tightening in May and uncertainty from Middle East tensions and potential El Niño effects, and said they were ready to act if expectations drifted. The currency appreciated in July–August before mixed moves in September, and a recent sovereign rating upgrade was expected to bolster sentiment compared with a year earlier.

item.title: The Cabinet approved a three‑month fuel relief programme and prices were revised at month‑end.
item.description: The plan earmarked Rs. 40.65 billion to cushion retail diesel and industrial grades from global spikes, with a monthly allocation that tapers from Rs. 15 billion in October. A subsequent decision set a Rs. 70 per litre subsidy on automotive diesel, while the State retailer raised petrol 92 by Rs. 15 to Rs. 414 and increased diesel and premium diesel as well. Energy import costs had surged after the Strait of Hormuz disruption, with crude above $100 a barrel and petroleum typically near a fifth of the goods import bill. Officials said some distributors had curtailed supply and the State supplier was carrying a larger burden than earlier in the year.

item.title: The World Bank approved $110 million to rebuild roads damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.
item.description: The financing through its crisis window will repair and climate‑proof about 600 km of provincial and rural links that restore access to markets, schools and clinics. It extends an ongoing programme to $610 million and is expected to benefit over 830,000 people directly, support roughly 5,671 jobs, and help reconnect close to 22,000 farmers, after the storm caused an estimated $4.1 billion in nationwide losses. Works will include drainage upgrades and landslide protection to withstand more frequent extremes, aligning with a 2026–2030 country strategy that emphasises resilient infrastructure. Transport sector damage alone had been assessed at around $973 million, including roads and nearly 700 bridges.

item.title: The U.S. State Department reported that the investment climate remains challenging despite macro stabilisation.
item.description: The 2026 country review noted foreign direct investment of $1.06 billion in 2025, about 1% of output versus 3–4% typical of peers, with concerns over policy consistency, regulatory delays and stalled projects. It cited unimplemented large‑ticket ventures and contract renegotiations, even as constitutional guarantees allow full foreign ownership in most sectors. The analysis pointed to the need for a stronger “one‑stop shop,” better procurement transparency and utility reform to lower operating costs. It also observed that free‑trade agreements and trade facilitation could influence export‑oriented investors more than tax incentives alone.

item.title: Customs moved to a paperless declaration process from October 1.
item.description: Importers and agents must now submit entries and supporting documents with valid digital signatures, replacing physical paperwork at submission. The rollout, developed with the public‑sector modernisation bureau and GovTech (a government technology unit supporting digital services), includes tamper‑evident checks and is intended to cut processing time and opportunities for fraud.

item.title: A driver demerit‑points pilot covering 33 specified offences began on October 1.
item.description: The six‑month trial, scheduled to run through March 31, 2027, complements online fine payment via Gov‑Pay and applies on expressways and major corridors. Authorities said permanent implementation would follow evaluation and public awareness after the test period.

item.title: A court granted bail to a sitting legislator in a financial‑crime probe connected to aircraft procurement.
item.description: The magistrate set cash and surety conditions, imposed a travel ban and warned against witness interference, following investigative submissions that a charge sheet was in preparation. The order came amid parallel proceedings in another high‑profile property transaction case in which investigators had told court they received foreign updates on suspect funds.

item.title: A new Metro Bus fleet of 112 vehicles was deployed on seven Western Province routes.
item.description: The launch followed a capital outlay of about Rs. 7.5 billion and included eight units provided by a bilateral partner, with plans to add 50 more before the April holiday period. Officials said the goal is to cut single‑occupancy car trips into the capital and expand to inter‑city services later with private participation.

item.title: Price controls on 13 high‑cost essential medicines saved an estimated Rs. 5.7 billion for the State.
item.description: The regulator said the saving was computed on capped items in the hospital basket and followed tighter oversight of large‑ticket therapies. The announcement came alongside plans to finance all public‑sector vaccines from domestic funds next year for the first time.
